questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **which**.

***__Key Points__**​​

__
 
• ​The pronouns that connect a clause or phrase to a noun or a pronoun, is called a relative pronoun.
 
• The most common relative pronouns are:
 
 
• who, whom, whose, which, that.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *We don’t know the person who donated this money.*
 
• *You need to tick the box which says yes.​*
 
 
 
• ​We use 'who/whose' in relative clauses to refer to people, and sometimes to pet animals. (refer to the above example)
 
• We use 'which' in relative clauses to refer to animals and things, to introduce defining and non-defining relative clauses.
 
• We use 'whom' if the noun/pronoun is the object of the verb in the dependent clause.
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *The uncle whom we met at the family reunion is coming to visit. *(The noun 'uncle' is the object of the verb met.)
 
• *The person with whom I spoke was able to help me. *(The noun 'person' is the object of the preposition with.)
 
 
 
• ​Since we are referring to **'**one of the ways' in this sentence, 'which' will be used in the **blank **part of the sentence.

 

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** ​

 
• ​​We use 'which' in relative clauses to refer to animals and things.
 
• Example: 
 
 
• You need to tick** the box** which says Yes.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence?**

Who killed Ravana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - By whom** ****was Ravana killed?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in an active voice form, hence we need to convert it into a passive voice form.
 
• We need to follow these instructions while changing the voice of an interrogative sentence.
 
 
• The preposition 'by' will commence the sentence.
 
• The objective case of the pronoun 'who' will be used now. (whom)
 
• The given sentence is in the simple past tense.
 
• The passive verb form for the simple past interrogative sentence: was/were + subject + past participle form of the verb.
 
• So, '**killed Ravana**' changes into 'was Ravana killed'.
 
 
 
• At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get- *By whom was Ravana killed?*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. One of the twins was driving better than the other.

B. Mahesh kept comparing them every day.

C. After two months of driving daily, finally both the twins were at par.

D. Mahesh was teaching the twins how to drive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - DABC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them:
 
 
• Sentence D introduces us to the subject 'Mahesh'. It is the introductory sentence and will be put in the first place.
 
• Sentence A tells us about **how the twins were going about learning to drive.** It will be put in second place.
 
• Sentence B tells us about Mahesh's attitude towards the twins. It will be put in third place.
 
• The last sentence is C as it mentions **the scenario after two months of learning.**

 
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct order is - **DABC**

The director wanted Aziz to play the role of the doctor __as well also__ that of the apprentice.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• An adverb is a word or phrase that modifies or qualifies an adjective, verb, or other adverb or a word group, expressing a relation of place, time, circumstance, manner, etc.
 
• **As well** is an **adverb **which means ‘**also**’, ‘**too**’ or **‘in addition’**. We usually use **'as well'** at the **end **of a **clause**.
 
• **As well as** is a multi-word **preposition **which means** ‘in addition to’.**
 
• Example:
 
 
• *We look forward very much to seeing you again and to meeting your wife **as well.***
 
• *When they go to Austria, they like walking** as well as** skiing.*
 
 
 
• As per the structures given above, the adverb '**as**' will replace '**also**' in the 1st option.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *The director wanted Aziz to play the role of the doctor **as well as** that of the apprentice.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Gary said, "I have finally cleared my exams with distinction!"

options.text: Gary said that he has finally cleared his exams with distinction.
Gary exclaimed that he had finally cleared his exams with distinction.
Gary exclaimed that he cleared his exams with distinction.
Gary told that he have cleared his exams with distinction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **Gary exclaimed that he had finally cleared his exams with distinction.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• When the direct speech is in an exclamatory form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• Convert the sentence in the direct speech into assertive.
 
• The tense of reported speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense. 
 
• The reporting verb said is converted into **exclaimed**.
 
• The pronoun 'I' is replaced by 'he' accordingly. 
 
• Similarly '**my**' will be replaced by '**his**' in the **latter **part of the sentence.
 
• The helping verb is changed according to the tense, followed by the 3rd form of the verb.
 
• The present perfect tense i.e. have cleared will be changed to the past perfect tense i.e. had cleared.
 
 
 
• ​​At last line up the remaining part.

 

Following these steps, we finally get- *Gary exclaimed that he had finally cleared his exams with distinction.*
